resources.string: Configure your Vespera (I / II / Pro), then connect.
Tap «Search Vespera instruments» to list nearby networks.
No saved instrument — pick one from the scan or enter SSID/BSSID.
SSID does not look like a Vespera (expected: Vespera-*, vespera2-*, VESPERAPRO-*).
Selected %1$s (%2$s). You can Connect Vespera now.
No instrument saved. Scan and select your Vespera (I / II / Pro).
Precise Location and Nearby Wi-Fi devices are required. Requesting permissions…
System location is OFF: enable Location, then search again. %1$s
Android limited/rejected a new scan. Showing the last result. %1$s
Scan updated. %1$d instrument(s) found — tap to save:
Last result. %1$d instrument(s) found — tap to save:
Cannot open Location settings on this ROM.
Select or save your Vespera (I / II / Pro) first.
No Vespera network available: connect first.
%1$s:%2$d does not respond on the Vespera network: %3$s
Connection lost%1$s. Previous IP/port are no longer valid until you reconnect.
Not connected%1$s. Previous IP/port are no longer valid until you reconnect.
Precise Location (and Nearby Wi-Fi) is required to search/connect the Vespera.
Permissions denied. Allow them in App settings, then Search instruments.
CONNECTED to Vespera (local network, no Internet)
Not connected to Vespera: cannot check Singularity.
Singularity does not see the instrument.
Vespera API unreachable: Singularity cannot connect.
System Wi‑Fi is not associated with the Vespera.
vespera-netd daemon missing or outdated (needs check-singularity).
Singularity is not running: launching it…
Singularity started and connected to the instrument.
Singularity launch failed: still not running.
Singularity missing instrument: refreshing route and restarting Singularity…
Singularity missing instrument: refreshing route (automatic restart waits 1 min)…
Singularity sees the instrument after route refresh.
Singularity sees the instrument after restart.
Singularity still missing the instrument after restart.
This tab configures the Raspberry Pi Ethernet cable (eth0).\nNeeded for weather, clock (NTP) and Telegram.
Choose DHCP (router assigns the IP) or a fixed manual IP.
Config applied, but the gateway has no Internet uplink. Check router/NAT on %1$s.
Config applied, but the default route is missing.
Daemon not responding (vespera-netd missing or stuck).
Port inventory: connect Vespera and tap «Verify ports».
Inventory updated. %1$d port(s) open (API not detected).
Live status on Socket.IO (8083). Commands sign the challenge with Ed25519 on REST (8082). Resume reuses the last target from status.
Power off telescope: OK — shutdown in progress, Wi‑Fi will drop.
Status has no challenge or telescope ID: cannot sign the command.
Status has no challenge: cannot sign the command.
No target to resume: start an observation in Singularity first, or wait until status shows RA/Dec.
Observatory coordinates are missing. In the System tab pick a city (or read coordinates from Vespera) and try again.
Starting auto-init; resume is sent as soon as init finishes…
Initialize unavailable: already initialized or tracking in progress.
The telescope is not plugged into mains power (running on battery). Accept to continue without more alerts until you plug it in, or Ignore: you will be asked again the next time you open this tab.
The hard disk is more than 80%% full (%1$s). Accept to continue without more alerts until usage drops below 80%%, or Ignore: you will be asked again the next time you open this tab.
No `vespera-*.swu` found in the app `files/` folder. Copy the SWU to the Pi and retry.
Open the picker and choose the `vespera-*.swu` file from disk or PC.
No file picker is available on this device.
Unable to read the selected file.

Update the instrument with `{ %1$s }`?

Size: %2$s
SHA-256: %3$s
Internal checksum: OK (%4$d files)

Use only a correct Vespera file. Wrong updates may leave the instrument unusable.
Blocked: battery is low (use mains power or >= 50%%).
Invalid SWU file (CPIO magic not recognized).
Close the arm and park the telescope?
Resume the observation (multi-night / last target from status)?
Telescope is not initialized. Run auto-init and then resume the multi-night observation?
Initialize the telescope? Current date/time and observatory coordinates (System tab) will be sent.

USER photos are copied to the HD first, then the Vespera powers off. The hard disk stays powered (auto USB cut often needs a physical replug to remount). Wi‑Fi will drop and Helper will lose the connection.
API unreachable on 8082/8083 (try Verify ports on the Connections tab).
Connect the Vespera from the Connections tab to read instrument status.
You can safely remove the HD
HD powered off. Tap “Activate HD” to wake and mount it (even with Vespera offline).
No disk selected. Refresh the list, pick the HD, then Mount.
No USB/SCSI disk found. Plug in the HD and refresh.
%1$d disk(s) found — tap to select, then Mount.
Select a disk from the list first.
HD unmounted. The disk stays powered until you tap Power off HD.
vespera-netd daemon missing or outdated (needs list-disks / mount-disk).
HD powered off: Vespera offline (no sync). Tap Activate HD to wake it, or it remounts when the telescope comes online.
HD powered off with the telescope.
HD powered off. Tap Activate HD to wake it.
No HD saved: after the first mount it remounts when Vespera is online.
Saved HD: %1$s (id %2$s) — auto-remount when Vespera is online.
Waiting. At night, when Vespera comes online, and before power-off, if the HD is ready, USER photos are copied, verified, then deleted on the instrument.
Automatic night sync every %1$s h. Daytime (%2$02d:00–%3$02d:00) has no schedule: it runs when Vespera comes online and once more before power-off.
The photos are on the Vespera: connect it from the Connections tab, then retry.
Sync OK: %1$d copied, %2$d already present, %3$d deleted on Vespera (%4$s).
Sync failed: %1$s — unverified files were not deleted.
Sync paused. Tap Continue in Helper to resume transfer, verify and delete.
Paused until %1$s (next schedule). Tap Continue to resume sooner.
Transfer, verify and delete keep running if you close Helper. Overlay permission keeps the progress popup visible over Singularity.
Overlay already allowed: progress stays on screen.
Resuming after interruption: checking state and completing…
Suspended transfer: waiting for Vespera to resume…
Telescope: no FTP port found on %1$s (trying 21, 2121, 2221, 8021)
Telescope: connect Vespera to search the FTP port
Hard disk: FTP off (starts when the HD is mounted)
Two FTP ports: telescope (live) and hard disk.
NTFS mount failed. Check that /data/local/tmp/ntfs/mount.ntfs is on the Pi.
HD powered off. You can unplug the USB cable or use Activate HD.
FTP listening on port %1$d (anonymous, delete allowed)
Next night sync: %1$s (every %2$s h). Daytime when Vespera comes online. Night ends at %3$s
Night sync overdue (due at %1$s, every %2$s h). Night ends at %3$s
USER folder missing on the Vespera.
HD not writable: USB bind lost. Tap Mount or retry after restarting the daemon.
Sync OK: %1$d downloaded, %2$d already present, %3$d deleted on Vespera, %4$d errors (%5$s)
Last sync: %1$s · OK (%2$d copied, %3$d already present, %4$d deleted)
HD not mounted. Mount it from VesperaHelper (Photos / Hard Disk tab), then retry.
%1$d items — tap a photo to swipe through them
Search a city: sunrise/sunset and NTP time (Ethernet) update on launch and every day, without Vespera.
Hours from sunrise/sunset in %1$s · night %2$02d:00–%3$02d:00. Night hours are edited on the Photos tab.
Hours are locked. Search a city again to restore automatic calculation.
Clock via NTP (Ethernet), without Vespera. Updated at launch and every day.
City time zone applied. NTP failed: Ethernet Internet is required.
Vespera has no GPS of its own (it gets location from Singularity) and currently exposes no coordinates. Search a city.
Sunrise/sunset cannot be computed at this latitude today.
Each item is a process the app runs on its own. Tick or untick the checks, then tap Save to apply them all.
About 30 min after sunrise, only the selected actions below run (order: sync → telescope → HD → Pi), regardless of telescope status.
Night every %1$s h. Daytime (%2$02d:00–%3$02d:00) when Vespera comes online and before power-off. Next: %4$s.
Sync when internal storage is full
During tracking, if internal photos are ≥%1$d%% a sync starts. Checked around :10 every hour.
Automatically continues a sync left unfinished (crash, close, pause).
Suspended work is waiting to resume.

With Vespera online (API/FTP), mounts the saved HD. No longer powers the HD off automatically (cutting USB often requires unplugging the cable to remount). Activate/Mount and Power off HD remain manual.
Sets the Pi time zone and clock via NTP on Ethernet/Internet, without Vespera. Runs only when Internet is up; at launch and about every 18 h.
Set a city in the Location section at the top.
When the Pi powers on, opens VesperaHelper and starts background services.
When the saved instrument appears on Wi‑Fi (or at boot), it connects on its own.
After the Wi‑Fi connection, starts Singularity in the background (about 3 s). Restarts stay on the button in the Connections tab.
Every 30 s, while the app is in the foreground, checks whether Singularity sees the telescope.
Serves copied photos from the HD over local FTP when the disk is mounted.
Restart services if the app is closed
If you swipe the app away, connection and sync services start again on their own.
Once a day, about 30 min after sunrise: runs the selected actions. Does not wait for GENERAL_SUN_TOO_HIGH.
Copy remaining USER photos to the HD before other actions.
Disabled automatically: cutting USB often prevents waking the HD without unplugging the cable. Use manual Power off HD only if you accept a physical replug.
Set a city (Location section, at the top) to compute sunrise.
last sync done, telescope powered off
After the other actions, also powers off the Raspberry Pi (root daemon).
City or coordinates for sunrise/sunset, NTP clock and weather.
Coordinates the instrument currently exposes (from Singularity: Vespera has no GPS of its own). Match within 100 m. If they differ, they can be sent with the same kind of command as park/init.
No dedicated GPS-set command. Coordinates are applied with Initialize (Telescope tab), like the other commands.
Use “Send location to Vespera” to try writing them to the instrument.
Vespera is not connected: instrument GPS cannot be read.
They do not match: about %1$d m apart (100 m threshold). Check the saved city or the location in Singularity.
The instrument is not exposing GPS coordinates right now. Vespera has no GPS of its own: location comes from Singularity.
Checks the weather at the Vespera location and, if rain is forecast soon, automatically closes and powers off the telescope.
When rain is forecast within the look-ahead: stop session → close Vespera → wait for arm retracted/CLOSED → verify → power off. Power off only happens after the closed state is confirmed.
Set a city or coordinates in the Location section at the top.
Location: uses city / lat-lon from the Position section above (synced).
Simulation active: no real command sent to the Vespera.

Create a bot with @BotFather, copy the token, send /start to the bot and get the chat ID (e.g. @userinfobot). Internet is required (Ethernet, VPN or LTE), not just Vespera Wi‑Fi. Save and pick events. One message per transition, checked every 2 minutes.
Enter token and chat ID, then Save.
Bot configured. Waiting for the first send.
VesperaHelper: running on battery (unplugged from mains).
VesperaHelper: rain forecast (%1$s mm within %2$d min) — starting telescope protection.
VesperaHelper: [simulation] rain forecast (%1$s mm within %2$d min) — protection not executed.
Set a city in System for the forecast.
